text.content: Skills represent learned knowledge, practical abilities, and proficiencies that characters acquire through training, experience, or study. Every skill is associated with a primary attribute (ST, DX, IQ, or HT) and has a difficulty level (Easy, Average, Hard, or Very Hard), which determines the cost in Character Points (CP) to learn and improve it.

A skill’s final level is based on its controlling attribute (e.g., DX, IQ). The character point (CP) cost to learn a skill depends on its difficulty (Easy, Average, Hard, or Very Hard) and the desired skill level relative to that attribute. For example, if you’re defaulting to a base attribute like IQ/Hard (IQ-6), roll 3d6 against the default level -- the controlling attribute minus the listed penalty (e.g., IQ-6). If the roll is less than or equal to that level, you succeed.

Instead of paying a cost per level, you pay a single, cumulative cost to buy the skill at a specific relative level. This makes it inexpensive to have a basic familiarity with many skills, while true mastery requires a significant investment.

Skill Point Cost Table

Skill Mechanics
Skill Level Relative to AttributeEasyAverageHardVery Hard
Attribute -3---1
Attribute -2--12
Attribute -1-124
Attribute +01246
Attribute +12368

Attribute +3461012
For each +1 level beyond +3+3+3+3+3

How to Use the Table: The table shows the total Character Point (CP) cost to learn a skill at a specific level relative to its attribute. To find the cost to improve a skill you already have, subtract the CP cost of your current level from the CP cost of your desired level. A dash means that level cannot be bought at that difficulty. The cheapest level the table prices is the lowest a skill can be taken at, and it always costs 1 CP: Attribute +0 for an Easy skill, Attribute -1 for Average, Attribute -2 for Hard, and Attribute -3 for Very Hard. Nothing exists between that level and the untrained default -- a skill with no points spent on it is not a skill you have, it is a default roll (see Defaults, below).

Example: A scoundrel with a Dexterity (DX) of 12 wants to learn the Stealth skill, which is an Average difficulty skill.

  • Untrained Default: The default is DX-5, which in this example gives a skill of 7. This costs 0 Character Points.
  • To get Stealth to 11 (DX-1): According to the table for an Average skill, reaching the level of “Attribute -1” requires a total investment of 1 Character Point.
  • To improve to Stealth to 12 (DX+0): The table shows the total cost for “Attribute +0” is 2 Character Points. This means the scoundrel spends one additional point (going from a 1-point total to a 2-point total) to raise the skill from 11 to 12.
  • To reach Stealth to 13 (DX+1): The table lists the total cost for “Attribute +1” as 3 Character Points. This costs one additional point to go from Stealth 12 to 13.
  • To master it at Stealth to 14 (DX+2): The total cost for “Attribute +2” is 4 Character Points, costing one more additional point.
  • To truly excel at Stealth to 15 (DX+3): The total cost for “Attribute +3” is 6 Character Points. The cost to advance from the previous level has now increased, requiring two additional points to go from 14 to 15.

It is important to note, one does not have to individually increment a skill as in this example. You could choose to go from the Untrained Default to “Attribute +3” by investing a total of 6 CP at once.

Defaults:Many skills have defaults, allowing a character to attempt a roll at a penalty if they do not possess the skill but have a related attribute or another skill. If you haven’t spent any points on a skill, you must use its default level.

Specialties: Some skills are broad and require a specific specialty (e.g., Engineer (Hyperdrive), Expert Skill (Jedi Lore)). Throughout this chapter, a † after a skill’s name marks a skill that must always be taken with a specialty — it cannot be learned as a single generic skill.

Cost: A specialty costs exactly what its parent skill costs: it has the same controlling attribute and the same difficulty, and is priced off the same table. Narrowing a skill’s scope does not make it cheaper -- Melee Weapon (Vibrosword) at DX+1 costs what Melee Weapon costs at DX+1, which is what Broadsword costs at DX+1. A bonus written against a specialised skill covers every specialty of it: where an item or trait grants "+1 to all Guns specialties" or "+1 to all weapon skills," it applies to each specialty the character has, not to one chosen at purchase and not to a bare unspecialised skill -- there is no such thing. A bonus naming an unspecialised skill, like Brawling, simply applies to that skill.

Bonuses: A bonus written against "all weapon skills" covers every skill that rolls to hit -- armed or unarmed, melee or ranged -- including Lightsaber Combat and Innate Attack, and every specialty of a specialised attack skill. It does not reach a skill that makes no attack roll: Fast-Draw and Shield sit in the same Combat Skills section and are untouched, as are Tactics, Armoury and the like.

All Weapon Skills: Anything else such an item grants is stated on its own, which is how @UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.Skjt6Gqhhw8BiF1Y]{Chapter 10} writes its stimulants -- Hyper-Battle Stimulant lists "+2 to all weapon skills" and "+1 to Parry/Block" as separate clauses, and Battle Stimulant names its Fright Check bonus separately from its weapon-skill bonus.

A Stated Penalty Beats the Default: Where a chapter gives the penalty for attempting one specific job without the skill that job needs -- @UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.9YXkSHXGYI6RwDtb]{Chapter 12}'s internal-component salvage at -3, or its whole-saber teardown at -4 -- that figure governs for that job and replaces the default above.

Skill by Skill: Read it skill by skill, not procedure by procedure: two skills that default to the same target rarely default at the same number, so a single stated penalty can override the default for one substitute and land on the same figure as another's by coincidence.

Worked Case: Lightsaber Construction is the worked case -- Armoury (Melee Weapons) defaults at -4 and Electronics Repair (Powered Melee) at -5, so a procedure printing “at a -4 penalty” for both is restating the default for the first and overriding it for the second in one clause. Where a procedure states no penalty, the defaults above apply unchanged.

Defaulting Between Specialties: A character trained in one specialty of a skill is not helpless with another. Any specialty of a skill defaults to any other specialty of that same skill at -2, and this beats the skill's own attribute default whenever it is higher -- a pilot who flies starfighters can handle a freighter badly, a rifleman can use a pistol badly, a mechanic who knows repulsorlifts can look at a hyperdrive. Take the better of the two.

Exceptions: This does not apply where the chapter says otherwise:

  • Metallurgy (Beskar) and Metallurgy (Phrik) each state that a general Metallurgy level does not carry over
  • Lightsaber Combat (Class Type) defaults between Class Types at -1 rather than -2 (see @UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.9YXkSHXGYI6RwDtb]{Chapter 12})
  • Guns defaults between its own specialties at a flat -1 (the Guns (Any)-1 convention).

Note that Lightsaber Forms are not skills at all -- they are schools of combat bought with Character Points, and are covered in @UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.BUSu7dFLs9IzOvPY]{Chapter 9}.

A character carrying a weapon or tool outside their specialty is legal and needs no extra points -- they simply take the -2.

Prerequisites:Some skills require a character to have a certain attribute level, another skill at a minimum level, or a specific advantage before they can learn it.

These skills govern a character’s effectiveness when violence is the answer

Axe/Mace (DX/Average)

  • Defaults: DX-5, Flail-4, or Two-Handed Axe/Mace-3.
  • Description: The skill of using one-handed axes, maces, and picks, including vibro-axes. Can be taken as a specialty of Melee Weapon.

Baton (DX/Average)

  • Defaults: DX-5, Shortsword-2, Broadsword-3, or Tonfa-3.
  • Description: The skill of using a short, one-handed impact weapon with no edge -- shock and stun batons, truncheons. Can be taken as a specialty of Melee Weapon (Baton).

Brawling (DX/Easy)

  • Defaults: DX-3.
  • Description: Proficiency in unarmed fighting, from bar-room brawls to disciplined martial arts. Covers punches, kicks, and grappling.

Broadsword (DX/Average)

  • Defaults: DX-5, Lightsaber-4, Jitte/Sai-3, Saber-4, Shortsword-3, Smallsword-4, or Two-Handed Sword-4.
  • Description: The skill for balanced, one-handed blades like ancient metal swords or certain vibro-swords. Can be taken as a specialty of Melee Weapon.

Echani Martial Arts (DX/Hard)

  • Defaults: DX-6, Brawling-4, Judo-3, or Karate-3.
  • Description: The fighting tradition of the Echani, who treat combat as a form of conversation. A practitioner reads an opponent’s weight shifts, breathing and micro-movements to know a strike before it is thrown, and answers it in the same motion. Fluid and precise rather than powerful, it is taught from childhood on Eshan and rarely well outside it. See “Anticipation” under Unarmed Combat Techniques in @UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.BUSu7dFLs9IzOvPY]{Chapter 9}.

Fast-Draw (DX/Easy)

  • Defaults: None
  • Description: A skill that lets characters quickly draw a weapon, or ammo/magazine/etc from a holster/sheath/pouch/etc.

Fencing (DX/Average)

  • Defaults: DX-5, Melee Weapon-5
  • Description: The ability to deflect incoming attacks with precision. Limited ability rendered ineffective by carrying large weapons, or large shields.

Flail (DX/Hard)

  • Defaults: DX-6, Axe/Mace-4, or Two-Handed Flail-3.
  • Description: The skill of using flexible weapons like nunchaku or heavy combat flails.

Gunner (DX/Easy)†

  • Defaults: DX-4 or IQ-5.
  • Description: The skill of firing aimed, turreted weapons, such as those found on starships, ground vehicles, and fixed emplacements. Requires a specialty (e.g., Gunner (Turbolaser), Gunner (Ion Cannon)).

Guns (DX/Easy)†

  • Defaults: DX-4 or IQ-5.
  • Description: The ability to operate, maintain, and accurately fire personal ranged weapons. This is the primary skill for any dedicated gunslinger. Requires a specialty matching the weapon’s form factor and power source together -- blaster and slugthrower versions of the same form factor are mechanically different enough to need separate specialties, though a Heavy variant of a form factor is still wielded identically to its standard version and shares the same specialty. The specialties are:
  • Guns (Blaster Pistol) -- blaster pistols, hold-out blasters, disruptor pistols, and their Heavy-tier variants
  • Guns (Blaster Rifle) -- blaster rifles, carbines, disruptor rifles, sniper-configured rifles, and their Heavy-tier variants
  • Guns (Blaster Heavy Weapons) -- tripod-mounted, shoulder-braced, or vehicle-mounted heavy blasters and repeating blasters, structurally distinct from a braced rifle or pistol
  • Guns (Slugthrower Pistol) -- projectile-firing pistols
  • Guns (Slugthrower Rifle) -- cycler rifles and other projectile rifles
  • Guns (Gauntlet) -- wrist-mounted launchers
  • Guns (Bowcaster) -- Wookiee-pattern draw-and-fire weapons, mechanically distinct enough from a standard rifle to need their own specialty
  • Guns (Explosive Launcher) -- grenade and rocket launchers.
  • Guns (Any)-1 lets a generalist use any of the above at a flat -1, per the same convention used for Lightsaber Combat.

Jitte/Sai (DX/Average)

  • Defaults: DX-5, Broadsword-3, Lightsaber-4, Main-Gauche-4, or Shortsword-3.
  • Description: The skill of using a pronged parrying weapon.

Judo (DX/Hard)

  • Defaults: DX-6.
  • Description: A form of unarmed combat focused on throws and grappling to use an opponent’s momentum against them. A more defensive alternative to Brawling.

Karate (DX/Hard)

  • Defaults: DX-6.
  • Description: A disciplined form of unarmed striking with hands and feet, allowing for more damaging and precise blows than standard Brawling: a character striking with Karate adds +1 per die of thrust damage at Karate DX+1, and +2 per die at DX+2 or higher (@UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.JJ04T5LHImjlILs1]{Chapter 7}).

Knife (DX/Easy)

  • Defaults: DX-4, Lightsaber-3, Main-Gauche-3, or Shortsword-3.
  • Description: The specific skill of fighting with small blades, from simple combat knives to vibro-daggers. Can be taken as a specialty of Melee Weapon (Vibro-knife).

Liquid Projector (DX/Easy)

  • Defaults: DX-4.
  • Description: the skill to use a weapon that projects a stream of liquid or gas.

Main-Gauche (DX/Average)

  • Defaults: DX-5, Jitte/Sai-4, or Knife-4.
  • Description: The skill of using a knife or dagger in the off-hand, primarily for parrying and defense.

Melee Weapon (DX/Average)†

  • Defaults: DX-5.
  • Description: Proficiency with a specific category of non-lightsaber melee weapons that doesn’t fit any dedicated melee weapon skill defined in this chapter. Requires a specialty (e.g., Melee Weapon (Vibro-knife), Melee Weapon (Vibrosword), Melee Weapon (Shock Gauntlet)).
  • One Skill, Two Names: Where a dedicated skill’s own entry says it can be taken as a specialty of Melee Weapon, the two are one skill under two names, not two skills that default to each other: a character who bought Melee Weapon (Vibrosword) and a character who bought Broadsword each use their full level on that weapon, and neither pays twice. A character takes one name or the other, never both -- holding both would be holding one skill at two levels. Where a sheet already carries both, the higher level is the character’s level in that skill and the lower purchase was wasted.
  • Aliases: Such a name is an alias, not a specialty: the dedicated skill’s own difficulty and cost govern, because it is that skill. Melee Weapon (Vibro-knife) is Knife, so it prices as DX/Easy, not as Melee Weapon’s DX/Average.
  • True Specialties: Only a name with no dedicated entry of its own -- Melee Weapon (Shock Gauntlet) -- is a true specialty, priced off its parent. The dagger on Melee Weapon marks only that it can never be bought bare; a sheet may legally hold either form.

Polearm (DX/Average)

  • Defaults: DX-5, Spear-4, Staff-4, or Two-Handed Axe/Mace-4.
  • Description: The skill of using long, heavy shafted weapons with a striking head, like a vibro-halberd.

Saber (DX/Average)

  • Defaults: DX-5, Broadsword-4, Shortsword-4, or Smallsword-3.
  • Description: The skill of using a light, one-handed curving blade.

Shield (DX/Easy)

  • Defaults: DX-4 or Brawling-4.
  • Description: The skill of using a physical shield for defense. This includes personal energy shields that are handheld, as well as riot shields and ancient metal shields.

Shortsword (DX/Average)

  • Defaults: DX-5, Broadsword-3, Lightsaber-4, Jitte/Sai-3, Knife-4, Saber-4, or Smallsword-4.
  • Description: The skill of using a balanced, one-handed blade 1-2 feet long.

Smallsword (DX/Average)

  • Defaults: DX-5, Saber-3, or Shortsword-4.
  • Description: The skill of using a light thrusting blade.

Spear (DX/Average)

  • Defaults: DX-5, Polearm-4, or Staff-4.
  • Description: The skill of using spears, from primitive wooden spears to high-tech force pikes (that are not lightsabers).

Staff (DX/Average)

  • Defaults: DX-5, Polearm-4, or Spear-4.
  • Description: Covers fighting with any sort of staff or long stick, including the weapons of the Gand and the non-powered staves used by some guards.

Teräs Käsi (DX/Hard)

  • Defaults: DX-6, Brawling-4, Judo-3, or Karate-3.
  • Description: “Steel Hand” -- the lethal unarmed discipline developed by the Followers of Palawa expressly to fight Force-users. Its practitioners train to mask intent and commit to a blow only at the last instant, so that precognition has nothing to read. Closely held and rarely taught, it has been studied by a handful of Jedi and dark-siders alike. See “Steel Hand” under Unarmed Combat Techniques in @UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.BUSu7dFLs9IzOvPY]{Chapter 9}.

Tonfa (DX/Average)

  • Defaults: DX-5, Baton-3, Jitte/Sai-3, or Shortsword-3.
  • Description: The skill of using a side-handled baton for striking and forearm defense, such as the CorSec Stun Tonfa. Can be taken as a specialty of Melee Weapon (Tonfa).

Two-Handed Axe/Mace (DX/Average)

  • Defaults: DX-5, Axe/Mace-3, or Polearm-4.
  • Description: The skill of wielding long, heavy axes or mauls with both hands.

Two-Handed Flail (DX/Hard)

  • Defaults: DX-6, Flail-3, or Two-Handed Axe/Mace-4.
  • Description: The skill of using massive flexible weapons swung with both hands -- chain-flails, meteor hammers and similar weighted chains. Like all flails these are unbalanced, and cannot attack and parry in the same turn unless the wielder has 1.5x the weapon’s required ST.

Two-Handed Sword (DX/Average)

  • Defaults: DX-5, Broadsword-4.
  • Description: The skill for wielding large, heavy blades with two hands, such as ancient greatswords or large vibro-greatswords.

Thrown Weapon (DX/Easy)†

  • Defaults: DX-4.
  • Description: The skill of accurately throwing weapons, from knives and grenades to improvised projectiles. Requires a specialty (e.g., Thrown Weapon (Knife), Thrown Weapon (Grenade)).

Whips (DX/Hard)

  • Defaults: DX-6.
  • Description: The skill of using any flexible weapon made from a length of chain, leather, wire, etc. Can be used to entangle opponents (contested DX or HT vs. user’s skill), roll on every turn, releases opponent on success.

These skills represent a character’s physical conditioning and ability to navigate their environment.

Acrobatics (DX/Hard)

  • Defaults: DX-6.
  • Description: The skill of tumbling, balancing, and performing complex gymnastic feats, often used to entertain or to gain a tactical advantage in combat (e.g., bonuses to Dodge).

Body Language (Per/Average)

  • Defaults: Per-5 or Empathy-3.
  • Description: The skill of reading the posture, gestures, and expressions of others to discern their emotional state and intentions. Essential for interrogators and diplomats.

Climbing (DX/Average)

  • Defaults: DX-5 or ST-5.
  • Description: The skill of scaling vertical surfaces, from rock faces to the sides of buildings.

Dancing (DX/Average)

  • Defaults: DX-5.
  • Description: The skill of performing rhythmic and expressive movements, whether for artistic performance, social grace, or as part of a cultural ritual. Many Twi’leks are known to have innate grace, giving them a bonus to this skill.

Escape (DX/Hard)

  • Defaults: DX-6.
  • Description: The art of slipping out of bonds, handcuffs, or grapples.

Filch (DX/Average)

  • Defaults: DX-5.
  • Description: The skill of snatching, palming, and shoplifting small unattended objects without being noticed. Lifting an item from a person’s body is Pickpocket.

Flight (HT/Average)

  • Defaults: HT-5.
  • Description: The skill for maneuvering with natural wings or a personal flight system like a jetpack.

Forced Entry (DX/Easy)

  • Defaults: DX-4.
  • Description: The ability to kick in doors and windows, or demolish them with a crowbar, ram, or sledgehammer, without necessarily being adept at melee combat.

Holdout (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: IQ-5 or Sleight of Hand-3.
  • Description: The art of concealing weapons and gear on your person beyond what is allowed by the Concealment skill, especially against a pat-down search.

Innate Attack (DX/Easy)

  • Defaults: DX-4.
  • Prerequisites: Relevant Force Power (e.g., Force Lightning), or physical weapon augmentation (e.g., Integrated Blaster).
  • Description: Represents your trained or instinctual ability to aim and direct natural or built-in ranged powers. You must choose a specific specialization when you buy it (e.g., Innate Attack (Energy)).

Jumping (DX/Easy)

  • Defaults: DX-4.
  • Description: The ability to make controlled leaps, covering horizontal or vertical distances.

Distance: Jump distance comes off your Move, in yards -- the ground-speed figure you actually have after encumbrance, not the unmodified Basic Move. With a run-up of at least two yards you clear a horizontal distance equal to your Move; from standing, half that, rounded down; straight up, a third of the running figure, rounded down, minimum one yard. Make the Jumping roll to clear the full distance -- on a failure you cover half of it and land prone.

Encumbrance: Because the figure comes off Move rather than Basic Move, the Encumbrance Move Penalty (@UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.fZowiGenjFSpf9el]{Chapter 2}) is already applied by the time jumping reads it, along with anything else that raises or lowers your ground speed: a character loaded to Heavy encumbrance jumps as short as they run.

Bonuses: Bonuses to the Jumping skill improve the roll, not the distance. A flat bonus written as jump or jumping distance -- the Myomer Boost (Large) and the Baktoid “Enforcer” Leg in @UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.o2ZbGiux36xwNCw0]{Chapter 14} -- adds that many yards to all three figures, and is separate from any Move bonus the same item grants: a leg giving +1 Basic Move and +1 jump distance adds two yards to a running jump, not one, the first through the base figure and the second on top of it.

Multipliers: Multipliers apply last, to the finished figure: Super Jump (@UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.2I6Edey1uD2bgyES]{Chapter 4}) doubles it per level, and Force Jump/Leap (@UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.cvf2pB6RpI78AvBt]{Chapter 8}) multiplies it by its tier.

Running (HT/Average)

  • Defaults: HT-5.
  • Description: The skill for sustained overland running, essential for pursuits or long-distance travel on foot.

Sleight of Hand (DX/Hard)

  • Defaults: DX-6.
  • Description: The skill of tricking the eye with fast hand movements, used for magic tricks, cheating at cards, or planting an object on someone.

Speed-Reading (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: IQ-5.
  • Description: The ability to scan and absorb written information at a rapid pace.

Swimming (HT/Easy)

  • Defaults: HT-4.
  • Description: The ability to move effectively through water.

Vacc Suit (DX/Average)

  • Defaults: DX-5.
  • Description: The skill for operating within a sealed environmental suit or vacuum suit, including maneuvering in zero-gravity conditions.

These skills govern a character’s ability to interact with, manipulate, and lead other sentient beings.

Acting (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: IQ-5, Fast-Talk-3.
  • Description: The ability to convincingly portray a role, impersonate others, or feign emotions to deceive an audience. While a social skill, it is fundamentally a performance art.

Carousing (HT/Average)

  • Defaults: HT-0.
  • Description: The art of socializing in cantinas, bars, and clubs. Success can lead to valuable contacts, rumors, or simply a good time.

Detect Lies (Per/Hard)

  • Defaults: Per-6 or Psychology-4.
  • Description: The skill of spotting falsehoods by observing a subject’s speech patterns, body language, and physiological reactions.

Diplomacy (IQ/Hard)

  • Defaults: IQ-6, Fast-Talk-4, or Leadership-4.
  • Description: The art of negotiation, mediation, and statecraft. It is the key skill for reaching peaceful agreements, forging treaties, and representing a faction’s interests.

Expert Skill (Varies)

  • Description: This skill represents deep, specialized knowledge in a field not covered by other skills. It has no default.
  • Example: Expert Skill (Jedi Lore) (IQ/Hard) covers knowledge of the Jedi Code, history, and traditions.
  • Example: Expert Skill (Sith Lore) (IQ/Hard) covers knowledge of Sith philosophy, forbidden rituals, and ancient history.

Fast-Talk (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: IQ-5.
  • Description: The skill of bending the truth and weaving convincing lies to get out of trouble or gain an advantage.

Gambler (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: Mathematics (Statistics)-5 or IQ-5.
  • Description: The ability to read opponents, calculate odds, and win at games of chance over a sustained period.

Heraldry (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: IQ-5.
  • Description: The skill of identifying noble houses, military divisions, corporate logos, and other symbols of power and allegiance by their emblems.

Intimidation (Will/Average)

  • Defaults: Will-5 or Acting-3.
  • Description: Using threats, displays of force, or sheer presence to cow others into submission or extract information.

Interrogation (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: IQ-5, Intimidation-3, or Psychology-3.
  • Description: The skill of extracting information from a resistant subject through questioning, psychological pressure, or intimidation.

Leadership (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: IQ-5.
  • Description: The ability to inspire confidence, direct troops in combat, and command respect from subordinates.

Market Analysis (IQ/Hard)

  • Defaults: IQ-6 or Merchant-4.
  • Description: The study of galactic markets, trade routes, and corporate trends. Essential for large-scale economic planning.

Merchant (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: IQ-5 or Market Analysis-3.
  • Description: The skill of buying and selling goods, haggling prices, and assessing the value of cargo.

Politics (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: IQ-5 or Leadership-4.
  • Description: The skill of navigating and influencing governmental and bureaucratic systems, understanding power dynamics, and using procedures to your advantage.

Propaganda (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: IQ-5 or Psychology-4.
  • Description: The art of creating and disseminating information to shape public opinion on a massive scale.

Public Speaking (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: IQ-5.
  • Description: The skill of delivering speeches, addressing crowds, and making persuasive arguments to a group.

Research (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: IQ-5.
  • Description: The skill of effectively finding information from archives, libraries, computer networks, and other large repositories of data.

Savoir-Faire (IQ/Easy)†

  • Defaults: IQ-4.
  • Description: Knowing the proper etiquette, customs, and protocols of a specific social group. Requires a specialty (e.g., Savoir-Faire (Military), Savoir-Faire (Noble Court), Savoir-Faire (Corporate), Savoir-Faire (Underworld)).

Streetwise (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: IQ-5.
  • Description: Knowledge of the criminal underworld, including how to find black markets, deal with smugglers, and navigate the unwritten laws of the street.

Teaching (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: IQ-5.
  • Description: The ability to effectively impart knowledge and skills to students.

These skills are essential for spies, assassins, and anyone who prefers to operate from the shadows.

Camouflage (IQ/Easy)

  • Defaults: IQ-4.
  • Description: Using available materials to blend into the surroundings.

Concealment (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: IQ-5.
  • Description: The art of hiding objects—or oneself—on one’s person, in a room, or within a vehicle to avoid detection.

Disguise (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: IQ-5.
  • Description: Altering your appearance, mannerisms, and voice to pass as someone else. This is a key performance skill for spies and undercover agents.

Pickpocket (DX/Hard)

  • Defaults: DX-6.
  • Description: The ability to steal a purse, knife, etc., from someone’s person, or to “plant” something on them.

Shadowing (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: IQ-5.
  • Description: Following a target discreetly through various environments without being noticed.

Stealth (DX/Average)

  • Defaults: DX-5.
  • Description: The ability to move silently and remain unseen, crucial for infiltration and ambushes.

These skills represent a character’s education, analytical abilities, and specialized knowledge.

Administration (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: IQ-5.
  • Description: The skill of managing organizations, overseeing logistics, and navigating bureaucracy.

Animal Handling (IQ/Average)†

  • Defaults: IQ-5.
  • Description: A skill that allows one to train and work with animals. Requires a specialty by type of animal.

Archaeology (IQ/Hard)

  • Defaults: History (any)-5.
  • Description: The study of past cultures through their physical remains.

Area Knowledge (IQ/Easy)†

  • Defaults: IQ-4.
  • Description: Having detailed knowledge of a specific city, planet, or region, including its layout, key figures, and hidden places. A specialty is required (e.g., Area Knowledge (Coruscant Underlevels)).

Astronomy (IQ/Hard)

  • Defaults: Navigation (Astrogation)-5.
  • Description: The scientific study of stars, planets, and celestial phenomena.

Bioengineering (IQ/Hard)

  • Defaults: IQ-6.
  • Description: The skill to engineer living organisms with specific characteristics, or to create biotechnological products.

Chemistry (IQ/Hard)

  • Defaults: IQ-6.
  • Description: The study of matter, chemical compounds, and synthesizing materials. Essential for handling advanced poisons or crafting synthetics.

Crewman (IQ/Easy)†

  • Defaults: IQ-4.
  • Description: The skill to serve as crew aboard a specific type of large vehicle. Requires a specialty by vessel type (e.g., Crewman (Seamanship)).

Criminology (IQ/Hard)

  • Defaults: IQ-6.
  • Description: The systematic investigation of crime scenes, analysis of forensic evidence, and understanding of criminal psychology.

Cryptography (IQ/Hard)

  • Defaults: IQ-6 or Mathematics-3.
  • Description: The skill of creating and breaking codes and ciphers.

Current Affairs (IQ/Easy)†

  • Defaults: IQ-4.
  • Description: Keeping up with recent events, political shifts, and notable figures. Requires a specialty (e.g., Current Affairs (Galactic Politics), Current Affairs (Outer Rim Territories), Current Affairs (Underworld)).

Diagnosis (IQ/Hard)

  • Defaults: First Aid-5 or Physician-5.
  • Description: The skill of identifying diseases and medical conditions in living beings.

History (IQ/Hard)†

  • Defaults: IQ-6, Archaeology-5, or Bard-3.
  • Description: Knowledge of past events. Requires a specialty (e.g., History (Galactic Republic), History (Sith Empire)).

Housekeeping (IQ/Easy)

  • Defaults: IQ-4.
  • Description: The skill to manage, clean, and organize a household, or living space.

Investigation (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: IQ-5.
  • Description: The ability to gather information through records, gossip, interviews, and crime scene analysis.

Law (IQ/Hard)†

  • Defaults: IQ-6.
  • Description: Knowledge of the legal codes and procedures of a specific government. Requires a specialty (e.g., Law (Republic), Law (Hutt Cartels)).

Linguistics (IQ/Very Hard)

  • Defaults: IQ-7.
  • Description: The analytical study of the structure of language itself, which can help in deciphering unknown tongues.

Mathematics (IQ/Hard)

  • Defaults: IQ-6.
  • Description: Understanding of advanced mathematical principles, essential for physics, engineering, and cryptography. Can specialize in a particular field like Mathematics (Statistics), or Mathematics (Physics).

Meditation (Will/Hard)

  • Defaults: Will-6.
  • Description: The skill to calm the emotions, control the mind, and relax the body. Using meditation typically involves concentrating for several seconds, then rolling vs Meditation. On a success, a character can enter a trance-like state, which can be maintained for hours.

Metallurgy (IQ/Hard)

  • Defaults: IQ-6.
  • Description: The science of metals, their properties, and how to refine and work them. Covers common and rare alloys like Durasteel and Plasteel at your general skill level. Beskar and Phrik are different matters entirely -- each requires its own specialty, Metallurgy (Beskar) or Metallurgy (Phrik), bought and leveled separately from your general Metallurgy; your default skill level does not apply to either, the same way Guns (Blaster Pistol) does not let you fire a Blaster Rifle at full skill. Metallurgy (Beskar) is traditionally taught only within Mandalorian clans -- a non-Mandalorian learning it needs a real story reason (an apprenticeship, a clan mentor, adoption into a clan), not just spent character points.

Naturalist (IQ/Hard)

  • Defaults: IQ-6.
  • Description: Expert knowledge of the flora and fauna of a specific environment or planet.

Navigation (IQ/Hard)†

  • Defaults: IQ-6.
  • Description: The skill of plotting a course from one point to another. Requires a specialty (e.g., Navigation (Astrogation), Navigation (Planetary), Navigation (Urban)).

Observation (Per/Average)

  • Defaults: Per-5.
  • Description: the skill of observing dangerous or “interesting” situations without letting others know that you are watching, often from a distance. It can be used to counter Camouflage, Disguise, Filch, Pickpocket, Sleight of Hand, and Stealth.

Philosophy (IQ/Hard)†

  • Defaults: IQ-6.
  • Description: The study of fundamental questions about existence, knowledge, values, and reason. Requires a specialty (e.g., Philosophy (Jedi), Philosophy (Sith)).

Physician (IQ/Hard)

  • Defaults: IQ-7, First Aid-11, or Veterinary-5.
  • Description: General medical practice, diagnosing ailments, prescribing treatments, and long-term care.

Physiology (IQ/Hard)

  • Defaults: Diagnosis-5, Physician-5, or Surgery-5.
  • Description: the study of the human body and its function. Different species requires specialization.

Physics (IQ/Very Hard)

  • Defaults: IQ-7.
  • Description: The study of the fundamental laws of the universe, essential for advanced technology and force field engineering.

Poisons (IQ/Hard)

  • Defaults: Chemistry-4 or IQ-6.
  • Description: The skill of identifying, creating, and applying toxins.

Professional Skill (DX or IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: DX-5 or IQ-5.
  • Description: A realistic job skill that is more useful for making a living than for adventuring. Examples: Professional Skill (Shipwright), Professional Skill (Journalist), Professional Skill (Welder).

Psychology (IQ/Hard)

  • Defaults: IQ-6.
  • Description: Understanding the motivations, behaviors, and mental states of sentient beings.

Surgery (IQ/Very Hard)

  • Defaults: First Aid-12, Physician-5, Physiology-8, Veterinary-5.
  • Prerequisites: First Aid, or Physician.
  • Description: using invasive medical techniques to treat sickness or injury. It has optional specialization. Equipment and physiology modifiers apply; -3 if the area or equipment cannot be properly cleaned and sterilized; -3 for head or chest surgery; -5 for undiagnosed problems. If you lack Physician skill, you are at -5 to do anything but “field-expedient” surgery (e.g., stitch wounds or extract arrowheads, bullets, and shrapnel).

Survival (Per/Average)†

  • Defaults: Per-5.
  • Description: The ability to find food, water, and shelter in hostile wilderness environments. Requires a specialty (e.g., Survival (Desert), Survival (Forest), Survival (Tundra)). A day’s Survival roll can also forage a group’s meals (@UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.QD9SOsp2PLsi7llq]{Chapter 1}: Eating Well).

Tactics (IQ/Hard)†

  • Defaults: IQ-6.
  • Description: The skill of planning and executing strategies in combat, from small-unit ambushes to large-scale fleet engagements. Requires a specialty matching the combat domain (e.g., Tactics (Ground) for vehicle and infantry warfare on land, Tactics (Naval) for water-based vessel combat, Tactics (Space) for starship and fleet combat, Tactics (Small Unit), Tactics (Galactic), Tactics (Underworld)).

Tracking (Per/Hard)

  • Defaults: Per-6.
  • Description: The ability to follow physical trails and interpret signs left by people, creatures, or vehicles.

Traps (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: IQ-5 or Demolitions-3.
  • Description: The skill of detecting, disarming, and setting non-explosive traps.

Veterinary (IQ/Hard)

  • Defaults: Animal Handling (any)-6, Physician-5, or Surgery-5.
  • Description: The ability to care for a sick or wounded animal. There is an option to specialize in a particular type of animal. +5 if the animal knows and trusts you; -2 or worse if the animal is of an unfamiliar type.

These skills govern the creation, repair, and operation of technology, from simple tools to complex starship drives.

Architecture (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: Engineer (any)-4.
  • Description: The skill of designing buildings and other large structures.

Armor (DX/Easy)†

  • Defaults: DX-4.
  • Description: Trained familiarity with moving, fighting, and staying steady in a specific weight class of armor, reducing how much it saps your stamina. On a successful roll when you don a suit of armor for the day, treat your Encumbrance Level (see @UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.fZowiGenjFSpf9el]{Chapter 2}) as one category lower for the purpose of calculating your EP cost only -- it does not change your actual carried weight, Basic Lift, or Move.
  • Specialties: Requires a specialty: Armor (Light), Armor (Medium), or Armor (Heavy), matching the weight classes in @UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.sM4JaeipflPpOZgw]{Chapter 13}. A specialty only helps with armor in that weight class; a character trained in Armor (Light) gets no benefit while wearing heavy armor.
  • Untrained Wear: Wearing a weight class you have no specialty in is clumsy rather than impossible: Medium armor imposes -1 DX and Heavy imposes -2 DX for as long as it is worn. Light armor imposes no penalty -- anyone can manage a padded vest. These penalties are flat and need no roll; buying the matching specialty removes the penalty and opens Trained Efficiency (@UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.JJ04T5LHImjlILs1]{Chapter 7}). The penalty keys on holding the specialty, not on the donning roll, so a character who lacks it takes the -1 or -2 whether or not that roll succeeds.

Armoury (IQ/Average)†

  • Defaults: IQ-5 or Engineer-4.
  • Description: The skill of performing routine maintenance and field repairs on weapons and armor. For extensive customization or fabrication, see the Armstech skill below. No skill for design; for that, see Engineer. Requires a specialty covering one category of gear: Armoury (Small Arms) for pistols and rifles, Armoury (Heavy Weapons) for heavy/repeating blasters, Armoury (Blasters) as a broader catch-all for the whole blaster family, Armoury (Melee Weapons), Armoury (Body Armor), Armoury (Cybernetics), or Armoury (Explosives).

Armstech (IQ/Hard)†

  • Defaults: IQ-6. Branch-specific defaults and prerequisites are listed with each branch below.
  • Description: A master craftsman’s knowledge of building and modifying advanced weapons and armor from the ground up, fusing traditional smithing with materials science and micro-electronics. This is the skill for ground-up creation and deep customization; for routine maintenance and field repairs see Armoury, and for design see Engineer. Lightsabers are not built with this skill -- see Lightsaber Construction.
  • Specialties: Requires a specialty matching the skill the finished item is wielded or worn with, so that the person who uses a thing and the person who builds it name it the same way. The wielding skill decides, never the item’s name: a Shock Gauntlet is wielded with Melee Weapon (Shock Gauntlet), so it is built with Armstech (Shock Gauntlet), while Armstech (Gauntlet) covers the wrist-mounted launchers wielded with Guns (Gauntlet). Two items sharing a word in their names are not one specialty.
  • Defaults and Prerequisites vary by branch and are listed with each below.
  • Ranged Weapons: Specialties match Guns’ own (this chapter): Armstech (Blaster Pistol), Armstech (Blaster Rifle), Armstech (Blaster Heavy Weapons), Armstech (Slugthrower Pistol), Armstech (Slugthrower Rifle), Armstech (Gauntlet), Armstech (Bowcaster), Armstech (Explosive Launcher). A master gunsmith’s knowledge of building advanced ranged weapons from the ground up. Defaults: IQ-6, Armoury (Small Arms)-4, Armoury (Heavy Weapons)-4, Electronics Repair (Blasters)-5, or Metallurgy-5. Prerequisite: Armoury (Small Arms) or Armoury (Heavy Weapons), Electronics Repair (Blasters).
  • Liquid Projectors: Armstech (Liquid Projector), matching the Liquid Projector wielding skill (this chapter), covering the advanced construction of flamethrowers and similar weapons. Defaults and Prerequisite as for Ranged Weapons.
  • Melee & Thrown Weapons: Specialties match the melee skill the weapon is wielded with (this chapter): so a vibro-axe is built with Armstech (Axe/Mace), a vibrosword with Armstech (Broadsword), a Mandalorian Meteor with Armstech (Two-Handed Flail), and so on for every melee skill this chapter defines. The rule generates the list; it is not limited to the examples given. A weapon wielded under Melee Weapon (X) is built with Armstech (X).
  • Thrown Weapons: A thrown weapon follows the same principle: one that also has a melee profile is built with that melee specialty -- a throwing knife is Armstech (Knife), a javelin Armstech (Spear) -- while a purpose-built thrown weapon with no melee profile takes a specialty matching Thrown Weapon’s own (this chapter), such as Armstech (Grenade).
  • A master craftsman’s knowledge of building custom vibro-axes, shock-staves, and other complex weapons.
  • Defaults: IQ-6, Armoury (Melee Weapons)-4, Electronics Repair (Powered Melee)-5, or Metallurgy-5.
  • Prerequisite: Armoury (Melee Weapons), Electronics Repair (Powered Melee).
  • Armor: Specialties match the Armor skill’s own (this chapter), being the weight classes of @UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.sM4JaeipflPpOZgw]{Chapter 13}: Armstech (Light), Armstech (Medium), Armstech (Heavy). Expertise in designing, fabricating, and modifying advanced personal armor -- laminate plates, energy-dispersive underlays, and integrated systems such as shield generators and sensor suites. Defaults: IQ-6, Armoury (Body Armor)-4, or Electronics Repair (Sensors)-5. Prerequisite: Armoury (Body Armor).
  • Heavy-Tier Variants: A specialty can also work on a Heavy-tier variant of its own form factor at a -4 penalty (e.g., Armstech (Blaster Pistol) attempting a Heavy Blaster Pistol’s internals) -- the wielding skill is identical, but the internal engineering of a Heavy variant is different enough to warrant the penalty when it isn’t your specialty’s main focus. Armstech (Blaster Heavy Weapons) itself works on any Heavy blaster variant at full skill, since that is specifically its area of expertise.

Brewing (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: Cooking-4 or IQ-5.
  • Description: The art of making alcoholic beverages, from Corellian ale to Tatooine moonshine.

Computer Operation (IQ/Easy)

  • Defaults: IQ-4.
  • Description: The basic use of computer systems, including accessing public datapads, searching the HoloNet, and operating standard shipboard terminals. For illegal access, see Security.

Computer Programming (IQ/Hard)

  • Defaults: IQ-6.
  • Description: The skill to write and debug computer software.

Cooking (IQ/Easy)

  • Defaults: IQ-4.
  • Description: The ability to prepare palatable and nutritious food. A prepared meal can leave those who eat it Well-Fed (@UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.QD9SOsp2PLsi7llq]{Chapter 1}: Eating Well).

Demolitions (IQ/Hard)

  • Defaults: IQ-6.
  • Description: The safe handling, placement, and detonation of explosives, as well as the disarming of enemy charges.

Driving (DX/Average)†

  • Defaults: DX-4.
  • Description: Operating ground-based vehicles. Requires a specialty (e.g., Driving (Land Speeder), Driving (Repulsor-Tank), Driving (Swoop Bike)).

Electronics Operation (IQ/Average)†

  • Defaults: IQ-5.
  • Description: Operating complex electronic equipment. Requires a specialty. The ones this book uses are Comms, Computers, Security, Sensors, Media, Medical, Power Systems, Industrial (for heavy machinery), Blasters (for power cells, emitters and firing chambers), Powered Melee (for vibro-generators and shock emitters), Droids, Cybernetics, Starship Systems, Weapon Systems, Electronic Warfare and Force Fields. A GM may allow others; these are simply the ones the equipment chapters call for by name.

Electronics Repair (IQ/Average)†

  • Defaults: IQ-5.
  • Description: The skill of diagnosing and repairing damaged electronic devices. Requires a specialty matching those in Electronics Operation.

Engineer (IQ/Hard)†

  • Defaults: IQ-6.
  • Description: The skill of designing, building, and performing major overhauls of complex systems. Requires a specialty (e.g., Engineer (Hyperdrive), Engineer (Starship), Engineer (Weapons Systems), Engineer (Droids)).

First Aid (IQ/Easy)

  • Defaults: IQ-4.
  • Description: The skill of providing immediate medical care, stopping bleeding, setting bones, and stabilizing critically wounded patients until advanced medical attention is available.

Force Field Technology (IQ/Very Hard)

  • Defaults: Electronics Repair (Force Fields)-4, Physics (Force Fields)-4, or IQ-7. Prerequisite: Electronics Repair (Force Fields).
  • Description: A highly specialized skill representing a deep understanding of protective energy fields. A character with this skill can design, build, repair, and modify personal and vehicle-scale shield generators.

Forgery (IQ/Hard)

  • Defaults: Artist-4 or IQ-6.
  • Description: The skill of creating convincing fake documents, ID cards, and other credentials.

Free Fall (DX/Average)

  • Defaults: DX-4.
  • Description: The ability to control your body while falling, in zero-g, or during a parachute/repulsor-assisted drop. A successful roll lets you land from a fall or jump without injury (within reason -- this doesn’t save you from orbital drop velocities), stabilize yourself in microgravity to work or fight normally, or execute a controlled atmospheric descent. Failure means you take the fall normally, or tumble out of control in zero-g until you can grab something or the GM allows another roll.

Knot-Tying (DX/Easy)

  • Defaults: DX-4, Climbing-4, Crewman (Seamanship)-4.
  • Description: The skill to tie a wide variety of knots quickly and efficiently.

Lockpicking (DX/Average)

  • Defaults: DX-5.
  • Description: The art of opening mechanical locks without the original key.

Machinist (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: IQ-5, Armoury (any)-4, or Engineer (any)-4.
  • Description: The skill of operating machine-shop tools -- lathes, mills, presses, cutting torches -- to cut, shape, and fabricate raw materials into precise structural parts and housings. Used alongside or in place of Armoury for the mechanical fabrication portions of crafting (frames, chassis, housings), though it lacks Armoury’s specialized knowledge of weapons and armor specifically -- the two overlap but aren’t interchangeable for every task.

Mechanic (IQ/Average)†

  • Defaults: Engineer-4 or IQ-5.
  • Description: The skill of repairing and maintaining machinery. Requires a specialty. The ones this book uses are Droids, Cybernetics, Starship, Hyperdrive, Power Core, Life Support and Industrial. A GM may allow others; these are the ones the equipment and vehicle chapters call for by name.
  • Examples: Mechanic (Hyperdrive), Mechanic (Cybernetics), Mechanic (Life Support), Mechanic (Droids).

Pharmacy (IQ/Hard)

  • Defaults: Chemistry-5 or IQ-6.
  • Description: The science of compounding and dispensing medical drugs, from simple kolto packs to advanced combat stims.

Piloting (DX/Average)†

  • Defaults: DX-4.
  • Description: Operating vehicles in three-dimensional space, including atmospheric and space flight. Requires a specialty (e.g., Piloting (Starfighter), Piloting (Freighter), Piloting (Speeder Bike)).

Robotics (IQ/Hard)

  • Defaults: IQ-6.
  • Description: The science of designing and programming autonomous mechanical bodies, sensors, and their motive systems.

Scrounging (IQ/Easy)

  • Defaults: IQ-4.
  • Description: Finding useful items, spare parts, or resources in scrap heaps, battlefields, and abandoned areas.

Sewing (DX/Easy)

  • Defaults: DX-4.
  • Description: The skill to work with fabric.

Slicing (IQ/Very Hard)

  • Defaults: IQ-7.
  • Description: The skill of bypassing security systems. This covers both electronic “slicing” (bypassing computer security, decrypting files) and defeating physical systems like mag-seals and laser grids. Attempting to slice without any gear inflicts a -5 penalty.

Smith (IQ/Average)†

  • Defaults: IQ-5.
  • Description: The skill of crafting, or forging weapons, armor, and associated items. Requires a specialty (e.g., Smith (Swords), Smith (Blasters), Smith (Guns), Smith (Mandalorian Weapons), Smith (Mandalorian Armor)).

This category covers skills used for creation, entertainment, and expression.

Artist (IQ/Hard)

  • Defaults: IQ-6.
  • Description: The skill of creating works of visual art, this could include painting, sculpture, holo-sculpting, or creating intricate calligraphic works. A successful roll produces a work of quality, while a critical success might create a true masterpiece.

Bard (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: IQ-5 or Public Speaking-2.
  • Description: The art of oral storytelling, captivating a crowd, and entertaining recitations.

Musical Instrument (IQ/Easy)†

  • Defaults: IQ-3.
  • Description: The skill of playing a specific musical instrument. Requires a specialty (e.g., Musical Instrument (Kloo Horn), Musical Instrument (Fizz)).

Singing (HT/Easy)

  • Defaults: HT-4.
  • Description: The skill of producing musical tones with the voice, from cantina performances to operatic arias.

Writing (IQ/Average)

  • Defaults: IQ-5.
  • Description: The skill of composing clear, persuasive, or entertaining text. This can be used to write anything from stirring political pamphlets and journalistic reports to poetry and epic ballads about the war.

These skills are exclusive to Force Sensitive characters and govern their ability to perceive and manipulate the Force. The use of these skills is often tied to specific Force powers. When in a role play scenario, you may roll to use Force skills without the expense of Force Points (FP) or Endurance Points (EP) as required by Force Powers.

Agility (DX/Hard)

  • Defaults: DX-6, Acrobatics-6, or Jumping-6.
  • Prerequisites: Force Sensitive.
  • Description: The ability to use the Force to augment physical movement ability (running, jumping, etc.)

Awareness (Will/Average)

  • Defaults: Per-5.
  • Prerequisites: Force Sensitive, Detect (Advantage)
  • Description: The ability to passively or actively scan surroundings for mental, spiritual, or physical changes.

Healing (Will/Hard)

  • Defaults: Will-6.
  • Prerequisites: Force Sensitive, relevant Force power.
  • Description: The ability to channel the Force to mend wounds, purge toxins, and restore vitality in living beings.

Influence (Will/Hard)

  • Defaults: Will-6.
  • Prerequisites: Force Sensitive, relevant Force power (e.g., Mind Trick).
  • Description: The skill of subtly manipulating the thoughts, emotions, and perceptions of others through the Force.

Lightsaber Combat (Class Type) (DX/Hard)†

  • Defaults: DX-6.
  • Prerequisites: Force Sensitive.
  • Description: The signature skill for wielding a lightsaber. Because a lightsaber can form a solid defensive barrier, this skill can be used for both Parry (vs. melee) and Block (vs. ranged). The calculated value for both defenses is (Skill/2) + 3. Note that successfully defending against blaster bolts specifically requires the Danger Sense advantage to anticipate the shot.
  • Requires a specialty (e.g., Lightsaber Combat (Standard), Lightsaber Combat (Shoto Standard), Lightsaber Combat (Lightwhip Standard), etc.) The specialty is the Class Type of the lightsaber the character intends to wield.
  • Class Type: Per @UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.9YXkSHXGYI6RwDtb]{Chapter 12}, the applicable Lightsaber Combat (Class Type) skill is determined by the combined classes of the Handgrip: Class Type = Emitter Class + Sleeve Class + Base Class. Where several of those classes share the same name, that name is added only once -- a Standard emitter, Standard sleeve, and Pike pommel give Lightsaber Combat (Standard Pike). For dual-bladed builds, the Class Type lists all unique class names across both sides in structural order (Emitter(s) > Sleeve(s) > Base).
  • Reading the Tables: @UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.9YXkSHXGYI6RwDtb]{Chapter 12}'s weapon tables print “Lightsaber Combat (Any)-1” in the Required Skill column because the table cannot know which Class Type a given character bought the skill in. Read it as the character's own Lightsaber Combat specialty -- whichever Class Type they took it in -- used at -1, the penalty applying because that specialty does not match the weapon's Class Type. A character who has bought no Lightsaber Combat specialty at all has nothing to use at -1, and falls back to DX-6.

Lightsaber Construction (IQ/Hard)

  • Defaults: IQ-6, Armoury (Melee Weapons)-4, or Electronics Repair (Powered Melee)-5.
  • Prerequisites: Force Sensitive, Lightsaber Combat-12+.
  • Description: The art and meditation of building a lightsaber from its core components. This involves gathering and attuning a kyber crystal, assembling the hilt, and aligning the emitter matrix. This requires a dedicated workbench and appropriate tools. Every part of a lightsaber falls under this skill -- handgrip components, Power Cells, Lens Assemblies, Emitter Matrices and the crystal itself -- whether you are building them, fitting them, or taking them apart again. Armoury and Electronics Repair do not cover lightsaber work; someone without this skill can only break a lightsaber down crudely, at a penalty, and forfeits any Force-attunement the components carried.

Movement (HT/Hard)

  • Defaults: HT-6.
  • Prerequisites: Force Sensitive
  • Description: The skill of using the Force to push one’s body beyond its natural physical limits, enabling superhuman feats of speed, agility, and leaping.

Sense (Per/Average)

  • Defaults: Per-5.
  • Prerequisites: Force Sensitive.
  • Description: The fundamental skill for perceiving the universe through the Force. It allows a user to detect presences, feel disturbances, sense emotions, and gain insights beyond the five conventional senses.

Telekinesis (Will/Hard)

  • Defaults: Will-6.
  • Prerequisites: Force Sensitive, relevant Force power (e.g., Force Push/Pull).
  • Description: The ability to manipulate physical objects and project kinetic force at a distance, from levitating small stones to blasting enemies off their feet.

Sith Sorcery (IQ/Hard)

  • Defaults: IQ-6.
  • Prerequisites: Alignment -75 or deeper, Force Sensitive.
  • Description: The ability to corrupt and mold The Force to alter reality itself, often in unconventional or unnatural ways through hand signs, incantations, rituals, or intense mental focus. Rare, but can be found in beings with an unconventionally deep connection to the Dark Side.
  • Era Note: Before 3959 BBY (see the Timeline Guide, @UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.bDmrWOfdGyX8KYB7]{Chapter 21}), no living Sith Master or Order exists to teach this skill -- it is learned only by piecing together fragments from Sith ruins, corrupted holocrons, and artifacts, making every practitioner before that date a self-taught cultist rather than a trained initiate.

Sith Alchemy (IQ/Very Hard)

  • Defaults: IQ-7.
  • Prerequisites: Alignment -75 or deeper, Force Sensitive.
  • Description: The ability to manipulate the physical world through The Force by twisting physical beings, or imbuing items, with intense, corrupting dark side energy. Like Sith Sorcery, it is rare, but can be found in beings with an unconventionally deep connection to the Dark Side.
  • Era Note: Before 3959 BBY (see the Timeline Guide, @UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.bDmrWOfdGyX8KYB7]{Chapter 21}), no living Sith Master or Order exists to teach this skill -- it is learned only by piecing together fragments from Sith ruins, corrupted holocrons, and artifacts, making every practitioner before that date a self-taught cultist rather than a trained initiate.

Languages are a trait of their own, tracked separately from skills -- a language is never rolled against IQ or priced off the skill table. Each is bought on the short fluency ladder below; your native tongue is free (see “Languages of the Galaxy,” below).

  • Language
  • Native tongues: Your native language(s) are free (see “Languages of the Galaxy,” below); Language is bought only for additional, non-native tongues.
  • Description: Fluency in one specific language beyond your native tongue(s). Buy it to the level matching how well you speak it:
  • Broken [1 point] (simple trade phrases, heavily accented, easily misunderstood)
  • Accented [2 points] (fully conversational, but unmistakably foreign)
  • Fluent [3 points] (indistinguishable from a native speaker).
  • Example: a character who wants to speak Huttese fluently buys Language (Huttese) at Fluent for 3 points.
  • Requires a specialty: Language (Huttese), Language (Shyriiwook), and so on.
  • Comprehension-only: A language you can understand but not physically speak (see Wookiees, below) only needs the Comprehension-only version, at half the normal cost, round up -- write it on the sheet as its own specialty, Language (Basic, Comprehension-only), so it is never mistaken for the spoken version. Halving the ladder above gives 1 / 1 / 2 points at Broken, Accented and Fluent (round up). A comprehension-only language a droid gets free from its programming (see Droids, below) costs 0 points and is written the same way; it is the only Language entry that is both comprehension-only and free.
  • Related Traits: Characters raised with more than one tongue take Bilingual or Polyglot (@UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.2I6Edey1uD2bgyES]{Chapter 4}); Language Talent (@UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.2I6Edey1uD2bgyES]{Chapter 4}) improves languages bought with points.
  • Language Requirement: Every character must know at least one language -- almost always their free native tongue(s) above, requiring no action or CP spend on the player’s part. The only exception is a character who is simultaneously unable to speak or hear conventionally (Deafness, Mute, or an equivalent trait), unable to read or write (Illiteracy), and unable to sign (typically requiring the loss or non-function of both hands or manipulators) -- an extremely rare stack of disadvantages (@UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.LHqDwyGfdwXUdoZO]{Chapter 5}) that a player must explicitly take together to justify a character with no language at all. Having just one or two of these -- Deaf but still able to write and sign, or Mute but still literate -- still satisfies the requirement through whatever channels remain open.
  • Languages of the Galaxy (Reference)
  • Galactic Basic Standard (“Basic”) is the trade and political lingua franca of the Republic -- the one tongue most crews, ports, and cantinas share. It is not, for that reason, free. Your one free language is your native tongue, written at Fluent for [0]; Basic sits on the ladder above like any other language and is bought unless Basic itself is your native tongue. For a Human -- and for anyone a player establishes as raised in or near Republic space -- that free native tongue is Basic. For a Chiss, a Twi’lek, a Gand, a Wookiee, or anyone whose heritage tongue is something else, the free native is that other tongue, and Basic, if the character speaks it at all, is bought (or taken as a second native with Bilingual, @UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.2I6Edey1uD2bgyES]{Chapter 4}).
  • What a native tongue costs, and what level it sits at: a native tongue is Fluent by definition -- the ladder above defines Fluent as “indistinguishable from a native speaker” -- so a free native language sits at Fluent and is written [0]. Every character has exactly one such free tongue unless a racial package or an advantage (Bilingual or Polyglot, @UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.2I6Edey1uD2bgyES]{Chapter 4}) grants another. Improving a language you already hold: subtract the cost of the level you hold from the cost of the level you want.
  • Basic, specifically: because Basic is so widely spoken, most spacefaring characters will want it even when it is not their native tongue. Three routes give it to them: buy Language (Basic) at the level spoken (the ladder above); take Bilingual (@UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.2I6Edey1uD2bgyES]{Chapter 4}) at character creation to hold Basic as a second native tongue for 1 point; or, with the GM’s agreement, declare the character Basic-native from the start and make their species tongue the bought or second-native one instead. None of these is free by default -- a non-Basic-native character who wants Basic pays for it one of these ways.
  • Accents and physiology are flavour, not price. Some species always speak Basic with an unmistakable accent (Rodian, Trandoshan), settle by habit at a limited fluency, or cannot physically produce it at all (Wookiee). These describe how a species sounds when it knows Basic; they never make Basic cheaper or free, and a permanent accent is colour, never a penalty.
  • Species and their native tongues: a character’s free native tongue is their species’ own language unless upbringing says otherwise -- Bothan speak Bothese, Chiss Cheunh, Twi’lek Ryl, Gand Gand, Miraluka Miralukese, Wookiee Shyriiwook, and so on, while Humans (and the Republic-raised) are native in Basic. The homeworld list below names the common tongues, and the Appendix carries the full master list of species and their native tongues. A character raised away from their people -- a Twi’lek brought up on Coruscant -- may instead take Basic as the free native and their heritage tongue as a bought or Bilingual language; that is the player’s call at creation.
  • Speaking Basic -- typical levels by species: the entries below are roleplay guidance for how well a species usually speaks Basic once it has learned it, not a discount. Basic is bought at these levels -- or any other -- on the ladder above.
  • Rodian (Rodese-first; Basic usually Accented rather than Fluent)
  • Trandoshan (Dosh-first; Basic often gutural and Accented)
  • Ugnaught (Basic usually Broken to Accented)
  • Weequay (Basic usually Broken -- short, direct phrases, which is what Broken means. They understand more than they say, but they do say it: this is spoken Basic at a low level, not the Comprehension-only entry a Wookiee gets. Their own tongue is Sriluurian; within-clan they also signal by untranslatable pheromones)
  • Quarren (Quarrenese-first; Basic ranges Broken to Fluent by individual)
  • Ithorian (Basic usually Fluent -- Ithorese’s dual-mouth vocalization gives it an unmistakable resonant cadence that no level of skill removes. The cadence is permanent flavour, never a penalty)
  • Selkath (Manaan’s isolation and unusual vocal apparatus mean Basic is uncommon among them -- most Selkath, Republic-facing officials included, speak it Accented at best and many not at all. A Selkath who speaks Basic bought it, deliberately, at the full ladder price)
  • Species for whom Basic is rare or impossible: Jawa (Jawaese and a trade-cant; Basic is rare, reserved for outsider negotiations, and a Jawa who has any bought it, Broken being where most who bother stop), Rakata (an ancient, isolationist pre-Republic remnant; native speakers of Rakatan with no Basic whatsoever, a genuine language barrier for the rest of the party to solve), and Wookiee (Shyriiwook-only -- see below).
  • Wookiees: A Wookiee’s vocal cords cannot physically produce Basic. A Wookiee who has learned Basic understands it but can only ever reply in Shyriiwook -- this is the Comprehension-only version of the trait (half the normal cost, round up), bought like any language, since not every Wookiee grows up with it. Full two-way conversation still needs a translator droid, a bilingual companion, or a patient audience.
  • Languages and Their Homeworlds: Basic (Coruscant), Arkanian (Arkania), Bothese (Bothawui), Catharese (Cathar), Cerean (Cerea), Chagri (Champala), Cheunh (Csilla), Devaronese (Devaron), Dosh (Trandosha), Durese (Duro), Gamorrese (Gamorr), Gand (Gand), Huttese (Nal Hutta), Ithorese (Ithor), Jawaese (Tatooine), Kel Dor (Dorin), Mando’a (Mandalore), Miralukese (Alpheridies), Mirialan (Mirial), Mon Calamari (Dac), Nautila (Glee Anselm), Nikto (Kintan), Quarrenese (Dac), Rakatan (Lehon, also called Rakata Prime -- see @UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.WoKoilSuw4eubRUd]{Chapter 19}), Rodese (Rodia), Ryl (Ryloth), Selkath (Manaan), Shyriiwook (Kashyyyk), Sriluurian (Sriluur), Sullustese (Sullust), Togruti (Shili), Zabraki (Iridonia), and the ancient Sith language (Korriban -- see below). Aqualish, Bith, Feeorin, Gran and Talz speak tongues that carry their species’ name. See the Appendix for the full master list of species and their native tongues, and @UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.WoKoilSuw4eubRUd]{Chapter 19}’s “Planets of the Old Republic” for the language(s) tied to any specific world.
  • The Sith Language(s), Specifically: What this book calls “Sith, Ancient” is the historical, ceremonial tongue of the Sith Empire that ruled from Korriban a thousand years before this era -- what a scholar like Kreia has actually studied, and what survives in ruins, holocrons, and ritual inscriptions across old Sith worlds. It is entirely different from Darth Nihilus’s own vocalizations (see “The rare exception,” below) and from whatever is spoken at Dromund Kaas, capital of the true Sith Empire hidden in the Unknown Regions under the Emperor -- a language no Language entry in this book currently covers, since that empire is meant to remain undiscovered for the default campaign era (see @UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.bDmrWOfdGyX8KYB7]{Chapter 21}’s timeline). A GM running a later-era campaign that reaches Dromund Kaas should feel free to introduce Sith, Imperial as a new specialty when that becomes relevant.
  • Droids: A droid’s language ability comes from its programming, not lived fluency, and works differently from an organic character’s. Every droid speaks Droidspeak (binary) natively and understands both binary and Basic; speaking Basic aloud, though, takes a vocabulator built for it. Protocol-model droids and any unit with a dedicated linguistic processor package are built knowing dozens to millions of languages simultaneously -- this is a built-in function of the chassis, not a Language purchase (see @UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.1ZEtj9W2Z8w75PYC]{Chapter 17}). Droidspeak -- the binary machine tongue droids use among themselves -- is a language in its own right, not a quirk. Only a minority of models -- protocol droids and other vocabulator-equipped units -- speak Basic aloud; a droid with no Basic vocabulator (astromechs, and most utility and combat units) understands Basic but answers only in binary, carrying Basic at Comprehension-only [0]. An organic can learn to understand binary the same way -- Language (Droidspeak, Comprehension-only), bought on the half-ladder above -- but can never physically produce it, the exact mirror of a Wookiee understanding Basic without speaking it.
  • The rare exception: A handful of beings speak nothing resembling a conventional language at all -- Darth Nihilus’s guttural, dark-side-warped vocalizations are understood by no Language entry in this book, native or learned; treat this as a unique trait (see his @UUID[Compendium.shadowbase.handbook.JournalEntry.WoKoilSuw4eubRUd]{Chapter 19} entry) rather than a language to be bought or learned.
